3. Being aggrieved, the government of Bangladesh filed First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 175 of 1992 before this court which was ultimately dismissed on 22.8.1994 along with others, 16 such appeals. Thereafter the decree-holder-petitioner filed Money Execution case No.40 of 1995 before the second court of the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka on 13.8.1995. Since the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka was delaying to make payment of the award money to the decree-holder on the ground that the requiring body did not place the necessary found, the decree-holder-petitioner filed an application before the Exciting court for attachment of the moveable property of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 23.1.2003. The learned Joint District Judge noticed that several adjournments were granted to the judgment-debtor Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to deposit the award money in executing court but without any result. In any view, the executing court rejected the prayer for attachment of the moveable properties of the Deputy Commissioner on the ground that there would be inconvenience in performance of the government functions. Accordingly, by the impugned order dated 13.10.2003 the prayer for attachment was rejected. 

 4. Being aggrieved thereby the decree-holder as petitioner moved this court and obtained the present rule. 

 6. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr. A.Y. Masihuzzaman and also perused the order passed by the Division Bench on 14.7.2004. On consideration of the materials placed before me "I am in full agreement with the decision of the Division Bench in respect of the facts and findings made there in holding that the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka is avoiding deposit of the award money despite several instructions sent to him by the learned Additional Attorney General Mr. J. Mohammad Ali who took time from this court also with an assurance that he would see that the Deputy Commissioner make deposit of the award money in court so that the decree-holder may get the award money within a reasonable time but all his attempts failed". Law requires that the executing court should take all possible steps to expedite payment of the decreetal amount to the decree-holder in order to see that the decree-holder gets the fruit of the decree after long standing litigation. The records placed before me show a poor and unfortunate activities of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka in not complying with the court's order by compelling the requiring body to place the fund in respect of the property which was acquired in L.A. Case No. 41/64-65. The concerned Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka did not perform his duty in accordance with law but all his actions delayed completion of the execution proceeding causing serious hardship to the decree-holder petitioner. It is unfortunate that the property of a citizen was acquired in 1964-65 but his award money has not yet been paid to him even inmid 2004. The Deputy Commissioner should not be allowed to slip over the matter for inordinate period at the cost and harassment of a citizen of country. I should express may desire that the concerned authority would look into the matter and do the needful so that this sort of harassment is not repeated in future. The convenience or inconvenience of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka should not be a ground to refuse the prayer for attachment, if law permits such attachment. The moveable property of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka should be placed under attachment within a period of 7 days from the date of the receipt of this order by opposite party No.1 Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka. The findings and observations made hereinabove indicate that the impugned order suffers from illegality and infirmity resulting in a serious miscarriage of justice and cannot be sustained.
